subject: Potential data exfiltration: request for IR plan and artifacts
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <security@finops.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lydia.park@finops.com
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual outbound traffic to external host (requesting IR plan)

Hey Karthik,

We observed a short window (approx. 04/24 22:30-22:45 PDT) of elevated outbound connections from your tenant's ingestion service to a previously unseen IP range. Nothing confirmed as exfil, but our SOC would like to request Redwood's incident response plan and any immediate mitigations you put in place.

Can you share: 1) your IR runbook for suspected data exfiltration, 2) a checklist of evidence artifacts you can provide (flow logs, S3 access logs, API keys rotated), and 3) an estimated timeline for an initial post-incident summary?

We need the artifacts for our internal SIG review and procurement risk team. Priority: high.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Security Operations Lead
FinOps Analytics

Attachment: network-flow-sample-20260424.csv (CSV, 2.3 MB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <security@finops.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual outbound traffic to external host (requesting IR plan)

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up and for sharing the sample flow export. We take this seriously. I've looped in Mina (Security) and Vivek (SRE) to lead evidence collection and an initial triage. High-level answers below; we'll follow with artifacts and an IR timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Quick answers:
- IR runbook: we have a documented IR plan covering containment, evidence collection, and customer notification. We'll attach the IR playbook and a tailored checklist for the kind of network/API artifacts you requested.
- Evidence we can provide: VPC flow logs, load balancer access logs, application request logs, object-storage access logs (S3), instance metadata, system auditd traces (if available), and a hash list of any suspicious binaries.
- Immediate mitigations: gates put on outbound egress from the ingestion cluster, temporary key rotation for service accounts used by the pipeline, and enabling additional packet capture on affected nodes.

Next steps: Mina will post the IR plan and checklist, and Vivek will coordinate a secure transfer method for the logs (we prefer a pre-shared Drive folder + expiring link). If you prefer an SFTP or pre-signed S3 share, tell us.

We will NOT share raw customer payloads without an approved data handling agreement. If you need specific data fields redacted, note that and we'll prepare a redacted package.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales (Security Customers)
Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <security@finops.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: IR runbook + evidence checklist (redwood_ir_plan_v1.pdf attached)

Alex / Karthik —

I've attached our IR runbook excerpt and a short evidence checklist that maps to SIG/SOC2 artifact expectations. Highlights:
- Containment steps (isolate node, revoke service tokens)
- Preservation (collect flow logs, snapshot volumes, export application logs)
- Chain-of-custody notes (who accessed what, timestamps)
- Communications plan (customer notification timeline, PR escalation if needed)

We'll provide:
- VPC flow logs & ELB access logs for 04/24-04/25 (CSV)
- Application request logs (redacted where necessary)
- Audit logs for service account key rotations (if rotated)

Attachments: redwood_ir_plan_v1.pdf, sig-evidence-matrix.xlsx

Secure transfer: we will upload artifacts to the shared Drive folder at the link below with viewer restrictions and a 14-day expiry. If your legal team needs a formal DPIA or additional agreement for customer data handoff, flag it now.

I can jump on a quick call now or tomorrow morning to walk through details.

-Min a Haddad
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <security@finops.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: lydia.park@finops.com
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IR runbook + evidence checklist (redwood_ir_plan_v1.pdf attached)

Thanks Mina — appreciate the fast follow. A few clarifications:
- We prefer a pre-signed S3 link with object-level encryption. Drive link is acceptable if it enforces viewer expiration.
- Please include proof of key rotation (audit log) if performed; that's required for our SIG review.
- For the initial post-incident summary, can you provide a 1-page timeline and next steps within 24 hours? That will be circulated to our procurement and security leadership.

We'll schedule a short triage call at 10:30 AM PDT tomorrow (I've tentatively set it). I'll confirm the dial-in.

Alex

Attachment: network-flow-sample-20260424.csv (included earlier)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <security@finops.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IR runbook + evidence checklist (redwood_ir_plan_v1.pdf attached)

Alex —

Following the triage call, here's what we delivered and the immediate timeline: 
1) Evidence upload: pre-signed S3 share created with server-side encryption (AES256). Link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-share/finops-20260425?X-EXAMPLE (one-time link, expires 72h). Files uploaded: network-flow-sample-20260424.csv, redwood_api_access_20260424.log (redacted), sig-evidence-matrix.xlsx.
2) Initial 1-page summary (attached inline below): short timeline, suspected vectors, containment steps taken, recommended next actions.
3) Next artifacts: full ELB logs and object-store access logs will be staged by EOD Apr 27; volume snapshots will be available for legal/forensic review under NDA.

Initial 1-page summary:
---
04/24 22:28 PDT — ingestion cluster spike in outbound connections observed by FinOps tooling (source: 10.4.12.8)
04/24 22:31 PDT — automated alert triggered; SRE rule scaled up monitoring, traffic filtered to denylist host range
04/24 22:35 PDT — service account tokens rotated for pipeline worker group; temporary egress blocks applied to affected subnets
04/24 23:10 PDT — packet capture collected for affected node; no large payloads observed in the sample capture
04/25 09:00 PDT — joint triage initiated with FinOps; artifacts shared over pre-signed S3 link
---

If you require a formal postmortem with root cause analysis beyond what we've provided, we'll schedule a follow-up once forensic analysis completes. Let us know if you need chain-of-custody documentation for the snapshots.

-Vivek
Director, SRE Operations
Redwood Inference
